title: Trapping of Micro Particles in Nanoplasmonic Optical Lattice
protocol: Set up the optical tweezer kit as per its manual.
Connect a 470 nm blue light emitting diode (LED) light source to the fluorescence module.
Replace the high numerical aperture (NA=1.25, magnification 100x) oil immersion objective with a long working distance microscope objective (focal length 3.6 mm, WD=10.6 mm, NA=0.5).
Remove the lens in the beam expansion section of the assembled kit to achieve loose focusing of the laser beam.
Turn on the power supply and current for the laser diode of wavelength 980 nm.
Use the charged coupled device (CCD) camera to align the laser beam properly.
Deposit 40 nm indium tin oxide (ITO) film on a coverslip of thickness 0.17 mm with sputtering.
Spin coat an 8 µm layer of positive photoresist with spin speed 4000 rpm and time 30 s using a spin coater.
Soft bake the sample at 90 °C for 5 min.
Align the sample with the photomask for marker and expose to UV light for 80 s in the mask aligner.
Soak the sample in the photoresist developer for 130 s.
Deposit a 2 nm layer of chromium onto the sample using thermal evaporation.
Deposit a 40 nm layer of gold onto the sample using thermal evaporation.
Soak the sample in acetone and place it in an ultrasonic cleaner operating at 43 kHz and 150 W for 5 min for lift off.
Spin coat a layer of e-beam resist PMMA 120K with spin speed 5000 rpm for 30 s on a spin coater.
Bake the sample at 160 °C for 3 min on a hot plate.
Spin coat another layer of e-beam resist PMMA 960K with spin speed 5000 rpm for 30 s on a spin coater.
Bake the sample at 160 °C for 3 min on a hot plate.
Use an e-beam writer to expose the e-beam resist with acceleration voltage 30 kV and dosage 400 C/cm².
Deposit a 40 nm layer of gold in a thermal evaporator.
Soak the sample in acetone and place it in an ultrasonic cleaner for 5 min for lift off.
Connect wires between the control port of the circuit board and the electronic control board.
Connect the wires between the output port of the circuit board and thermoelectrical cooling (TEC) element.
Place the TEC element on the sample stage with heat sinking.
Connect wires from the circuit board to 5 V power supply.
Use the forward-looking infrared camera to monitor the temperature to check if the thermoelectrical cooling is properly cooling down.
Calibrate measured temperature in the forward-looking infrared camera and resistance temperature detector (RTD) thermometer.
Place the RTD thermometer on a blank coverslip.
Apply a small amount of thermal paste onto the RTD thermometer to ensure proper thermal contact between the RTD thermometer and coverslip.
Change the output power setting of the electronic control circuit to TEC element by changing the duty cycle of pulse width modulation setting.
Wait for 3 min to make sure the steady state temperature is reached.
Read the temperature using the RTD thermometer.
Turn on the forward-looking infrared camera and monitor the temperature.
Repeat this at various output power settings to obtain the temperature calibration curve.
Dilute micro polystyrene particles of diameter 2 µm in deionized water in a microcentrifugetube with proper volume ratio.
Put the sample with nanoplasmonic array on the stage and turn on a 470 nm LED as the fluorescence light source, manually setting the power to 5 mW for bright field imaging.
Locate the nanoplasmonic array using the marker.
Align the sample to ensure the array is in the center of the region of interest on the computer screen.
Dispense 10 µL of the diluted micro particles of diameter 2 µm on the sample with a micro pipette.
Turn on the current supply to the laser diode of wavelength 980 nm to excite the plasmonic resonance of the array with power in the range ~1 mW to 10 mW.
Manually turn on the power supply to the electronic control board to cool down the sample to a steady state temperature ~4 °C.
Click the "record video" sequence in the viewer software to open the recording dialog.
Click the "record" button to start the video recording of the motion of micro particles at a frame rate of 10 frames/s over the sample under the influence of laser beam using the CCD camera.
Click the "stop" button to stop the recording.
